title: Foundation course
summary: A ten-week owner course. Each week needs at least five short practice days and an observable check before the next week opens.

cadence.sessionLength: Keep sessions short and end on a success. Blue Cross suggests about 2 to 5 minutes and one RSPCA branch page suggests about 5 to 15 (disc-007). This course does not collapse those into one number.
cadence.onFailedGate: Repeat the week at an easier version of the same skill.
cadence.maintenance: Give earlier skills a few repetitions in each later week. Week 10 takes one of them into a mildly new place.

alignment.basis: Week themes follow the public headings of IMDT's 2-day theory course, 4-day practical course, and assessed exercises, retrieved 2026-10-10. This is a lighter owner timetable, not those courses. Lesson wording is paraphrased from UK welfare-charity sources, not from IMDT course material.
alignment.disclaimer: Independent guidance. Not affiliated with or endorsed by IMDT Ltd, and not a professional qualification.

parts.title: Practise
parts.imdtAnalogue: 4-day practical course, exercises this registry can teach

parts.title: Real life
parts.imdtAnalogue: Behaviour modification and professional limits, owner version

weeks.title: How dogs learn
weeks.aim: Set up kind equipment, learn that behaviour repeats what pays off, and charge a marker before asking for new skills.
weeks.practice: Pair the marker with a reward on several days. Fit the collar, ID tag, and harness, and check the microchip record.

gate.summary: The dog looks for a reward when it hears the marker, across two sessions. Collar, ID tag, and harness fit are done.

weeks.ifGateFails: Keep pairing the marker with a reward. Do not add a new skill this week.
notes: Shock-collar status stays the cautious wording already in lesson-equipment-and-law (review-020).

weeks.title: Read your dog
weeks.aim: Get a reliable name response in a quiet place, and notice stress early enough to give space.
weeks.practice: Play the name game in a quiet room on several days. On one boring outing, watch for stress signs and do not add a training ask.

gate.summary: The dog orients within 2 seconds of its name, said once, at conversational volume, in low distraction. The owner can name stress signs and give space when they appear.

weeks.ifGateFails: Shorten the name game and drop distractions. The recall weeks stay closed until this check is met.

weeks.title: Plan the work
weeks.aim: Pick one goal, keep a diary, and use the same cue across the household.
weeks.imdtAnalogue: Class planning and a one-to-one consultation, owner version
weeks.practice: Log several short sessions against one written goal. Keep a few marker and name repetitions in each session.

gate.summary: One written goal exists, and several short sessions are logged against it.

weeks.ifGateFails: Shrink the goal to a single skill in a quiet room and log that.

weeks.title: Positions
weeks.aim: Teach sit, then down and a short stay, plus a hand touch. Build stay duration before distance.
weeks.imdtAnalogue: Down, nose to hand touch, and twist or spin
weeks.practice: One position at a time, indoors or in a quiet garden. Add the word sit as the dog sits. For the stay, add duration while you are still close (disc-006).

gate.summary: The dog sits on cue with the lure starting to fade, and holds a short stay close to the handler.

weeks.ifGateFails: Return to the lure sit in a quiet room. Leave down, stay, and hand touch until the sit is easy again.
notes: lesson-spin-trick is optional and does not gate the week.

weeks.title: Everyday manners
weeks.aim: Teach leave-it, then an open-palm leave and a fair-trade drop. Add jumping or steal-and-chase only when that is the live problem.
weeks.imdtAnalogue: Retrieve, drop and swap half only
weeks.practice: Closed fist first, then the open palm, then a toy swapped for something better. Use four-paws-on-the-floor or the steal lesson only if that problem is happening.

gate.summary: The dog backs off a closed fist before the treat is released, and lets go of a toy in a fair trade.

weeks.ifGateFails: Stay on the closed fist. Do not move the food onto an open palm yet.
notes: A full retrieve is not this week. The drop and swap is the part the registry can teach.

weeks.title: Coming back nearby
weeks.aim: Add one recall cue in an enclosed space, then practise at 5 metres on a long line.
weeks.practice: Same recall word for the whole household. Enclosed space first, then a 5 metre long line in low distraction. Reward the return, including a slow one.

gate.summary: One recall cue. The dog returns to within arm's reach on a 5 metre long line in low distraction.

weeks.ifGateFails: Go back to the name game and shorten the distance. Do not repeat the recall cue if the dog is unlikely to come.

weeks.title: Coming back at a distance
weeks.aim: Stretch the long-line recall to 10 metres with mild distraction. Add an emergency cue only after that check.
weeks.practice: One cue, 10 metres, long line, mild distraction. Stay on the line.

gate.summary: One recall cue. The dog returns reliably on a 10 metre long line with mild distraction. Emergency recall practice starts only after this check.

weeks.ifGateFails: Drop back to 5 metres and an easier place. Leave the emergency cue unused.
notes: Public off-lead stays locked for the whole course (safe-002, metric-off-lead-not-unlocked).

weeks.title: Loose lead
weeks.aim: Walk ten consecutive steps with a slack lead.
weeks.practice: Practise the researched loose-lead lesson for several short outings. Keep a few recall repetitions on the line as well.

gate.summary: Ten consecutive steps with a slack lead without the owner stopping.

weeks.ifGateFails: Practise fewer steps in a quieter place. Do not raise the step count to force the check.
notes: Good Dog must not overwrite ex-lead-loose from this course. goodDogExportStatus stays hold_until_method_review.

weeks.title: One situation
weeks.aim: Work one real-life branch for the week. Leave the other branches for later.
weeks.imdtAnalogue: Behaviour modification and rehabilitation, owner version
weeks.practice: Choose one branch below. Keep the branch's constraint for the whole week, and keep a few reps of an earlier skill.

gate.summary: One branch has been practised on at least five days, inside that branch's constraint.

weeks.ifGateFails: Stay on the same branch at an easier setup. Do not switch branches to escape a hard day.
notes: Aggression, severe fear, sudden change, and suspected pain stay on the referral path (safe-004).

weeks.title: Generalise and stop
weeks.aim: Take one earlier skill into a mildly new place, prepare for handling, and name what this course does not cover.
weeks.practice: Repeat one solid skill somewhere mildly new. Practise predictable touch for a vet visit at the dog's pace. Read back the diary and pick the next skill or place.

gate.summary: One earlier skill still works in a mildly new place. The owner can name the problems that belong with a vet or a behaviour professional rather than in this course.

weeks.ifGateFails: Return that skill to the last place where it worked, then try a smaller change of place.
notes: Muzzle training stays in human review (review-016) and is not a week.

branches.title: Puppy
branches.constraint: No public-ground walking before the vet says vaccination cover is enough. Carry the puppy until then.

branches.title: Newly rehomed dog
branches.constraint: Settling comes before harder skills. Eating and resting in the home is the aim this week.

branches.title: Adolescent dog
branches.constraint: Shorten the session and return to an easier version of a skill that used to work.

branches.title: Hard walks
branches.constraint: Vet check before behaviour-change work. This week is management and a referral, not a rehabilitation plan.

branches.title: Noise and fireworks
branches.constraint: Safe place, notice the signs, comfort and management. Severe panic is a vet and behaviour referral.

branches.title: Time alone
branches.constraint: Short absences only while the dog is coping. Stop lengthening absences if the dog is distressed (review-006).

notInCourse.reason: The mat settle lesson exists. This course uses the stay for duration. Mat target remains partial on the crash-course checklist and is not a week.
Held for human review (review-016). Not a week.
A full retrieve has no owner lesson. Week 5 teaches the drop and swap only.
Multi-dog households have no protocol. Point at a reward-based trainer via referrals.
Owner question oq-train-001 has no lesson. Until one exists, raise reward value or use play, and do not invent a protocol.

excludedExercises.reason: Research only, one US organisation source.
